SMTO-SCH-0010 — The Gateway address for this schedule contains private details

GUID: 4e845ae7-f597-4af3-96fc-73723ea851c9
Slug: schedule-secret-rejected
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The address of the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) for this schedule includes private details like a password or token. SMTO won't keep those in a schedule, so it wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and look at the address shown for the Gateway this conversation uses. The schedule copies that address, so this is where the private part comes from.
  2. If that address has a user name, password, or anything after a ? or #, ask the person who manages SMTO to set the Gateway up with a plain address. Sign-in details belong in the Gateway's own secure setup, not in the address a schedule keeps.
  3. Once the Gateway has a plain address, create the schedule again from the same conversation. Nothing was saved the first time, so creating it again won't make a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and appears on the Schedules page, and its runs reach the intended Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type a password or token into the prompt or the Gateway address to get the schedule saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Scheduled scope capture rejected gateway_url because it is malformed, lacks a supported scheme (http, https, outbound, local) or host, or contains userinfo, a query string or a fragment.

What this means

  • Captured gateway_url is malformed, lacks a supported scheme/host or contains userinfo, query or fragment. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Captured gateway_url is malformed, lacks a supported scheme/host or contains userinfo, query or fragment.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect only the route's URL components; this guard does not scan all schedule text for secrets.

How to fix it

  • Use a plain Gateway URL without user:password@, ?query or #fragment (events/scope.py scheduled_agent_scope) and keep authentication in the Gateway's supported private credential storage, for example by re-pairing the Gateway. Then create the schedule again from a conversation that uses that Gateway.
  • Use a valid credential-free Gateway URL without query/fragment and keep authentication in its supported private fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported HTTP/HTTPS/outbound route identifies the intended Gateway with credentials kept in private storage.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
